{{ cloudMsg }} {{ cloudReach }}

Policies, accounts, questions, acknowledgements and notifications now travel between every device the moment they change. No committing files.

Push this browser's data to Firebase
Use this once, from the machine that holds the real library, to seed the database. After that everything syncs by itself.
Until this is connected, every browser keeps its own copy — a policy you publish here never reaches an employee, and their questions never reach you. Three steps, about ten minutes, no code:
1
At console.firebase.google.com, create a project, then Build → Firestore Database → Create database (production mode, region eur3). In its Rules tab, paste the rules below and Publish. 
{{ rulesText }}
2
Then Project settings → Your apps → Web app. Copy the whole firebaseConfig block Firebase shows you and paste it here:
Build my firebase-config.js
{{ cfgMsg }}
3
Put the downloaded firebase-config.js in your repository, replacing the empty one, and commit. Reload the live site — this card turns green, and you press Push this browser's data once to seed the library.
{{ fileCardTitle }}

Firebase is doing this for you now. Only use the file below if you ever switch the database off — mixing the two can push an old library over the live one.

Policies, accounts, departments and categories live in this browser until you publish them. Download the file below and commit it to your repository as data/hub.json — everyone who opens the site then gets this library and can sign in on their own device.

Download data/hub.json
Do this each time you publish or change a policy or an account. Acknowledgements, questions and notifications stay on each person's own device until IT hosts a server.
{{ sharedMsg }}
Back up the hub

Everything lives in this browser. Export a JSON backup before you clear browsing data, or to move the hub to another machine.
